newsitem.title: USA: Son of U.S. vintner dies of mushroom poisoning.
newsitem.headline: Son of U.S. vintner dies of mushroom poisoning.

text.p: Sam Sebastiani Jr., a member of a leading California winemaking family, has died after eating poisonous wild mushrooms, a family spokesman said on Thursday. He was 32.
Sebastiani was admitted to a San Francisco hospital on Jan. 6, a day after eating wild mushrooms while on an excursion with friends in Santa Rosa near San Francisco.

Family spokesman Michael Coats said doctors considered a full or partial liver transplant but Sebastiani's condition was too serious. He remained in critical condition until his death on Tuesday night.
Sebastiani was the son of vintner Sam Sebastiani Sr., who founded Viansa Winery in Sonoma. The family also owns the Sebastiani Vineyards, founded by Sebastiani Jr.'s great grandfather.
Sebastiani Jr. was apparently poisoned by the Amanita phalloides mushroom, better known as the "death cap." Eating even a small piece of such a mushroom can cause liver failure.
At least eight other people have fallen ill in the San Francisco Bay area in recent weeks after eating death cap mushrooms, which sprout after heavy rain. The others are expected to recover.
